A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same SkyDiffusion work, with matching core equations and identifiable experiments. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or embedded supplement; separately referenced supplementary material is outside the available evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, cross-dataset transfer experiments, and component ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results, including evaluations on the newly introduced Ground2Aerial-3 tasks, in Section 5 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The core BEV transformation, diffusion conditioner, and DNCM lighting procedure remain. However, v3 omits v1's explicit semantic-segmentation filtering step for distorted multi-to-one BEV regions without establishing whether the procedure changed or its description was shortened. Calling lighting optional does not establish a new capability, since v1 already evaluated light-free operation.

E1.justification: v3 retains CVUSA, CVACT, and VIGOR-Chicago and adds evaluated Ground2Aerial-3 tasks covering Hurricane Ian damage, historical street/aerial imagery from 2007–2014, and simulated ground-to-UAV imagery from MatrixCity. These substantially broaden the represented environments and synthesis requirements. The earlier CVACT–VIGOR transfer scenario is absent from the supplied v3.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds SelectionGAN without semantic masks and an explicit ControlNet comparator across the retained benchmarks, while removing DreamBooth from the reported comparisons. ControlNet's CVACT numbers match v1's street-input ablation, but its role in the main comparison is new. I2I-Turbo matches the previously named img2img-turbo.

E3.justification: v3 reports a modified 4:1 VIGOR split separating satellite identities, changes CVUSA inputs from 256×1024 to 512×1024, and replaces lambda=15 with dataset-specific values: 2 for CVUSA/CVACT, 10 for single-view VIGOR, and 0 for multi-view VIGOR. Its main comparison excludes lighting adjustment and uses single-view VIGOR inputs. G2A-3 introduces random 5:1 splits. These are substantive reported setting changes.

E4.justification: The supplied v3 omits v1's bidirectional cross-dataset generalization study, CUT/Aerial Diff BEV ablations, and street-input-plus-lighting control. v3 Table 3 retains CVACT component tests and expands VIGOR controls to distinguish street input, single-view BEV, and multi-view BEV with and without lighting. Figure 7 retains and expands the earlier multi-view qualitative analysis.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or formal significance tests. Both present individual metric values without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds baseline and G2A-3 results, including UAV FID values of 32.11 for SkyDiffusion and 52.76 for ControlNet. Retained entries also change, such as CVUSA img2img-turbo/I2I-Turbo SSIM from 0.103 to 0.127. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as direct performance gains. The earlier light-adjusted CVACT results and multi-view VIGOR results survive in v3 Table 3 rather than being lost.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain equivalent curved-surface and projection relations, nearest-camera composition, feature encoding, DNCM mapping, and diffusion loss. Neither supplied PDF adds formal propositions or proofs. The revised lambda values change experimental settings rather than the mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: v3 makes G2A-3 a central contribution and extends the claimed applicability to disaster, historical, and UAV image synthesis. It drops v1's claim to be the first diffusion-based street-to-satellite method. The reported headline SSIM/FID improvements also change from 14.5%/29.6% to 8.67%/21.50% under revised comparisons.

C2.justification: v3 develops interpretations concerning disaster assessment and historical-image gaps, and attributes stronger UAV synthesis to greater cross-view overlap. It clarifies that lighting adjustment is independent and optional. Conversely, v1's explicit qualification about limited cross-city generalization caused by architectural differences and single-dataset training disappears with the transfer study.

D1.justification: v3 adds substantial dataset-construction information: source platforms, disaster filtering, image alignment, and six-camera panoramic rendering with UAV cameras at 20 metres. It omits v1's documentation of LUT augmentation and the lighting module's L1/L2 training losses. The project-link description changes from a promised code/model release to results and dataset information; actual online availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts from autonomous driving, reconstruction, and virtual reality toward remote-sensing applications, with new disaster, historical-imagery, and dataset references. v3 acknowledges concurrent geometry-and-text-guided diffusion work and replaces the blanket BEV novelty assertion with emphasis on limited multi-to-one research. The Zero-1-to-3/Zero123++ discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around broader ground-to-aerial applications. v3 introduces an explicit contribution list and a dedicated dataset section, consolidates the earlier dataset/setup discussion, and removes the standalone generalization section. Terminology and the title also change from street-to-satellite to ground-to-aerial synthesis.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the opening and framework diagrams, and moves the one-to-one/multi-to-one illustrations into Figure 2. It combines the standard benchmark comparisons, restructures the ablation table, and adds G2A-3 displays. The earlier cross-dataset and standalone lighting visualizations are absent from the supplied v3.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the central evaluation through an explicit lighting-free, single-view comparison, a direct ControlNet baseline, and a declared VIGOR split separating satellite identities. G2A-3 adds useful empirical breadth and construction details. These gains are tempered by losing cross-dataset validation, its generalization caveat, and lighting-training documentation, supporting a limited net improvement.
